newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday extended Friday's gain and analysts said the higher trade and post- price-fixing buying suggested the market, currently at 14,819.7 points, would top September's year high of 14,832.7 on Tuesday.
But they said there were not enough positive signals to help take the market much higher.
"We can beat the high, but maybe not decidedly, and 15,000 points might provide technical and psychological resistance," said Emil Onyszczuk of Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Analysts said firms' September earnings reports due next week would provide the next major signal.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose one percent to 14,818.7 points and turnover rose 24.2 percent to 132.5 million zlotys ($47.1 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 48 to nine with 21 stocks flat.

Analysts said Monday's news that food prices rose 3.7 percent from August's final third to September's final third might be taken neutrally by the market since September's inflation figure due next week, even if high, should beat last year's three-percent rise.
The government and central bank both predict year-on-year inflation around 19 percent after September, with the latter saying it preferred no near-term real interest-rate cut.

Analysts said top gainer construction firm Remak surged 9.9 percent after revising up first-half earnings 65 percent, while biggest loser food trader Rolimpex, down 9.4 percent, fell after revising down earnings to 12.9 million zlotys ($4.6 million) from 16.3 million zlotys ($5.8 million).

Continuous trade turnover was at 0.7 million zlotys ($0.3 million) with biggest mover steel trader Stalexport down 2.9 percent. Mass privatisation NFI units rose 5.3 percent in lower turnover and were up one percent in lighter live trade.
